A Mercedes-Benz spokesperson confirmed the ruling, reaffirmed the company's dedication to competition laws, and cited measures implemented to guarantee complete legal adherence. The Chinese regulator stated that Mercedes-Benz and its Jiangsu dealerships engaged in monopolistic behavior by setting minimum prices for E-Class and S-Class vehicles, along with specific replacement parts. Earlier reports from Xinhua indicated that Mercedes-Benz had also been penalized for price manipulation in after-sales services within China, a leading global market for international car manufacturers.

S4C's future funding, largely dependent on the television license fee, faces uncertainty as the UK government undertakes a thorough review of the BBC. David Davies, MP for Monmouth, told BBC Wales that S4C deserves "special" attention given its role in supporting the Welsh language. However, government sources have hinted that S4C should adopt similar cost-cutting strategies as the BBC. The Labour party voiced concerns on Thursday that BBC budget reductions could threaten S4C's financial viability. Culture Secretary John Whittingdale has assured MPs of his commitment to the channel "within the next couple of years" and plans to consult with S4C's leadership shortly. Mr. Davies, speaking on BBC Radio Cymru, affirmed the government's recognition of S4C's importance and its vital role in preserving the Welsh language. He also raised the possibility of the Welsh Affairs Committee, which he chairs, examining broadcasting issues, including S4C.

In August 1974, after the discovery of a body in Cockley Cley, near Swaffham, Norfolk, Norfolk Police are utilizing sophisticated techniques for a follow-up post-mortem. Det Ch Insp Andy Guy indicated that DNA extracted from the remains might link the woman to a living family member. The original post-mortem, carried out on the heath where she was found, estimated her age to be 23 to 35 years old. She was clothed in a pink 1969 Marks & Spencer nightdress and encased in a plastic sheet secured with rope. Detectives are particularly exploring the theory that she was "The Duchess," a Great Yarmouth escort believed to be of Danish origin who disappeared suddenly after being prominent in the local community.

The study investigated the impact of environmental stress on mate preferences by comparing male army cadets undergoing rigorous training with a control group, focusing on their attraction to different female body shapes. The findings revealed that the cadets in intense training were more attracted to women with larger body sizes. Dr. Carlota Batres, who led the research, proposed that this change is an adaptive strategy, favoring partners perceived as healthier and more fertile when conditions are challenging. She emphasized that mate preferences are adaptable and react to environmental cues, with the observed change lasting as long as the stressful environment continued. Dr. Batres posited that these adaptations could be beneficial, increasing the chances of pairing with individuals better equipped to endure illness or limited resources. Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Perfecto Yasay intends to raise the South China Sea dispute at the upcoming Asia-Europe Meeting (Asem) summit in Ulaanbaatar, starting Friday. Chinese Premier Li Keqiang will also be present at the two-day event. This summit is the first major multilateral diplomatic gathering since Tuesday's UN tribunal decision that invalidated China's expansive claims in the area. China has dismissed the ruling, maintaining that the tribunal lacked authority and reiterating its ongoing activities. The Asem summit will bring together 53 leaders from Asia and Europe, including representatives from Vietnam and Malaysia, both nations with competing South China Sea claims. It also signifies the first international conference for the new Philippine administration.

John McCormack, a 46-year-old truck driver, drove his articulated lorry for 30 miles after colliding with a car carrying three children on the A9, Perth Sheriff Court was told. As a result, McCormack was banned from driving for two years and ordered to perform 250 hours of community service. Prosecutor Rebecca Kynaston stated that prior to the collision, drivers heading north near the House of Bruar shopping center saw McCormack's lorry on the wrong side of the road, forcing them to swerve onto the verge to avoid accidents. Despite these near misses, the lorry subsequently sideswiped a car containing a couple and their three children.

Kim Little of Seattle Reign won the BBC World Service award, chosen by public vote as the second-ever winner. She beat out Gaelle Enganamouit (FC Rosengard), Amandine Henry (Olympique Lyonnais), Carli Lloyd (Houston Dash), and Becky Sauerbrunn (FC Kansas City). The 25-year-old Little was surprised and grateful, stating her desire for women's football to keep advancing. She received the award at her team's training ground on Tuesday. Mary Hockaday, Head of BBC World Service English, praised Little and acknowledged the significance of the year for women's football, while also reaffirming the BBC World Service's commitment to recognizing talented female footballers. Little has been recognized as Seattle's most valuable player.

Stafford Hospital faced severe accusations of neglect, with reports of patients drinking from flower vases and untrained receptionists triaging emergencies. Julie Bailey, who founded Cure the NHS following her mother's experience there, was recognized with a CBE for her campaigning. Helene Donnelly, the A&E nurse who revealed the problems, was awarded an OBE. Hospital mortality rates were demonstrably higher than expected between 2005 and 2008. Allegedly, patients endured extended waits, were refused pain medication, and were deprived of fundamental needs like food and hydration. Donnelly, having lodged nearly 100 complaints and given evidence at the public inquiry, stated she was extremely proud and honored to receive an OBE for her work in the NHS, despite the difficulties she had encountered.

The FCA found that credit card firms were disincentivized to help customers in persistent debt because these accounts generated significant profits. As a result, the FCA pushed for interventions to incentivize larger debt repayments. This conclusion stemmed from an analysis of five years of data covering 34 million credit card accounts, alongside insights from 40,000 customer interviews. The FCA's initial research highlighted uneven competition, with certain customers and products lacking personalized support. Credit card companies readily assisted customers with arrears due to the "extreme unprofitability" they posed, a proactive response absent for those making only minimum payments. Joanna Elson, leading the Money Advice Trust (which runs National Debtline), echoed the FCA's worry about the 1.6 million people struggling with finances by making minimum payments, frequently on multiple cards, while also recognizing the broader capacity of credit card companies to provide effective customer support.

Alex Brazier, the Bank of England's financial stability director, highlighted the concerning 10% annual growth of unsecured household debt – encompassing car loans, credit card balance transfers, and personal loans – which significantly outpaces the 1.5% rise in household incomes. During a speech at the University of Liverpool, Brazier cautioned that this rapid expansion of household debt jeopardizes borrowers, lenders, and overall economic stability. He further warned that High Street banks risk complacency regarding this escalating consumer debt, potentially causing a rapid deterioration in lending practices. David Dallimore, a childcare and early childhood development expert at Bangor University, is calling for major improvements in the education of three- and four-year-olds. During an appearance on BBC's Eye on Wales, he argued that Wales lacks a stable, long-term strategy for early years support. The Welsh government has indicated it will consider changes following a review of the upcoming Childcare Bill. Currently, all children in this age group are entitled to a minimum of 10 hours of education through the Foundation Phase. However, the allocation of these hours for three-year-olds and the determination of funding levels are managed independently by each of Wales' 22 local authorities. This localized system has resulted in considerable variations in service quality and flexibility throughout the country, creating a disjointed and uneven system.

Decommissioning 13 unused fire engines, idle for two years, would leave London with 142 vehicles and allow reallocation of funds to recruit additional firefighters for Fire Rescue Units. The Fire Brigades Union (FBU), however, contends that permanently eliminating these engines would be a "dangerous and reckless" move. The London Fire Brigade (LFB) has proposed three cost-saving measures, guaranteeing no station closures or staff reductions. The LFB maintains that it has consistently achieved city-wide response time targets even without the 13 engines, asserting that their reinstatement would only marginally decrease the first engine's arrival time by approximately four seconds. Meanwhile, London Assembly Member Andrew Dismore has presented an alternative proposal.

Dee Stitt, a well-known UDA member linked to Charter NI, received criticism for his remarks in a Guardian interview. Charter NI's board responded with a statement expressing "deep disappointment and great concern" about the article and promising an internal investigation. During the interview, Stitt described the North Down Defenders loyalist band as "our homeland security" and alleged government disregard for Northern Ireland. Charter NI, a community-based organization, had received a Â£1.7 million grant from the Northern Ireland Executive's social investment fund. SDLP MLA Nichola Mallon argued that Stitt could not remain as Charter NI's CEO, demanding his immediate departure and pointing out that Charter NI's statement acknowledged his ongoing position as CEO.

Probationary Police Constable Frances Tilley's career with Northamptonshire Police ended after she admitted to evading a train fare on a trip from Bristol Temple Meads to Castle Cary in Somerset last June. A disciplinary hearing at police headquarters concluded that Tilley, who had served less than two years, was guilty of gross misconduct and dismissed. The hearing, held at Wootton Hall, focused on Tilley's journey from Northampton to Castle Cary on June 22nd of the previous year, during which she neglected to buy a ticket for the final leg, even though colleagues described her as "diligent, professional and committed". Force solicitor Elizabeth Briggs stated that Tilley intentionally avoided purchasing a ticket for the Bristol to Westbury and Westbury to Castle Cary segments of her journey, despite having ample opportunities to do so.

On Sunday morning, a jewelry exhibition at the Carlton Hotel on the Croisette in Cannes was targeted in a major robbery. This incident marks the largest in a series of high-profile thefts in Cannes, famous for its film festival. The Carlton Hotel, ironically, was the setting for Alfred Hitchcock's "To Catch A Thief" (1955), a film about a jewel thief on the French Riviera. The robbery took place in the hotel lobby, where a Leviev diamond exhibition was being held. Local reports state that the thief fled with the jewels in a briefcase, and the owner's identity is still unknown. A Cannes police spokesperson noted that if the estimated value of the stolen jewels is confirmed, it would be the second-biggest jewelry heist in French history.

As White Hart Lane undergoes reconstruction, Tottenham Hotspur has been hosting its Champions League home matches at Wembley Stadium. However, their recent 1-0 defeat on Wednesday marked their second European loss at the national stadium this season. In response, manager Pochettino defended Wembley, calling it the best venue globally for football, while attributing the defeats to the team's poor play. Ahead of potentially using Wembley for all home games next season, Pochettino voiced his frustration with their performances, especially against Monaco and Bayer Leverkusen. He stressed the need to resolve internal problems and expressed regret over the team's failure to perform as expected. This loss to Leverkusen follows their previous 2-1 defeat to Monaco at Wembley in their opening Champions League fixture.

In a BBC debate held at the University of Lincoln prior to the EU referendum, a moderator lamented being "battered on both sides by half-truths, lies and scaremongering." The debate, scheduled for broadcast on Sunday, included UKIP's Jane Collins (arguing for Leave), Labour's Melanie Onn (supporting Remain), and journalist Robin Limb. A central point of contention was the EU's impact on the National Health Service. Collins, representing Yorkshire and Humber, described the UK's annual £675 million payment to EU health initiatives, compared to the £49 million received, as "an atrocity," arguing that Brexit would improve the NHS. She also proposed streamlining nurse qualification procedures and ensuring equitable pay for all NHS staff. Onn, the Member of Parliament for Great Grimsby, responded by:

Ranjit Singh Power, a Wolverhampton hotelier, disappeared last year while on a business venture in Punjab. Although a taxi driver confessed to the murder, BBC India's Sanjoy Majumder indicates that local law enforcement believes others were complicit. Power's family is desperate to uncover the complete truth surrounding his vanishing and is disappointed by the lack of communication from both the Foreign Office and Indian authorities. His brother, Amrik Singh Power, describes their persistent efforts to obtain answers, highlighting his repeated attempts to receive updates from the Foreign Office. Mr. Power was last seen on May 8th at the Amritsar airport in Punjab, and his family reported him missing after a week of silence. The taxi driver, Sukhdev Singh,

The University of Birmingham revealed in July the discovery of a 1,370-year-old Quran manuscript, which university spokesperson Susan Worrall called "a global treasure." The manuscript is free to view by the public on the Edgbaston campus until October 25. According to the university library, these pages of the Islamic text had remained unrecognized in their collections for almost a century. One visitor marveled at the find, speculating about the possibility that the Prophet Muhammad or his associates had handled it. Ms. Worrall, the director of special collections, described the discovery as "fantastically exciting," emphasizing that the university possesses one of the oldest Quran fragments known. Muslim leaders in Birmingham have expressed their delight at the find, including Muhammad Afzal, chairman of Birmingham Central Mosque, who shared his feelings after viewing the manuscript.

After Alastair Cook stepped down after four years as captain, Joe Root from Yorkshire was chosen to take his place as Test captain. Root and his new vice-captain, Ben Stokes, both stressed that the team would concentrate on winning games while also playing an exciting brand of cricket. Root, who is 26 years old and was previously the vice-captain, will captain his first game on July 7th against South Africa at Lord's. Stokes, a 25-year-old all-rounder from Durham, is now the vice-captain, and he emphasized how important Test cricket is and how much he wants to get people interested in it again. He promised to do everything he could to win and said that his new job wouldn't change who he was or how he played because he was still committed to helping the team in every way he could.

Speaking to troops stationed in Siachen, the world's highest battlefield between India and Pakistan, Prime Minister Modi asserted that their unwavering commitment guarantees India's security. Subsequently, he traveled to the flood-ravaged Kashmir valley, where severe flooding had claimed at least 281 lives, submerged Srinagar, and displaced over a million individuals. This visit is only the second time an Indian Prime Minister has visited Siachen, with Manmohan Singh's visit in 2005 being the first. Since India's control began in 1984, the harsh climate of the glacier, where deployments reach heights of 22,000 ft (6,700m), has resulted in more soldier fatalities than combat. Modi's visit, coinciding with the Diwali festival, involved discussions with senior authorities and relief personnel to evaluate the progress of aid operations. The September floods in Indian-administered Kashmir caused damage to roughly 180,000 residences, leaving a significant number of people still living in relief camps.

The Elephant and Castle nightclub, a popular venue in south-east London, has been fighting the construction of a residential building across the street, concerned that noise complaints from future residents could force its closure. Southwark Council initially blocked the development, but Boris Johnson overturned the decision. Liberal Democrat councillors who voted against the project faced criticism for not disclosing substantial donations their party had received from the nightclub during the planning meeting. These donations were unknown to both Labour councillors and the developer, Oakmayne, until the BBC exposed them. The council's legal advisor also warned the councillors that their failure to declare the donations could be unlawful. Both Ministry of Sound and the Lib Dems insist that their conduct was above board. In a letter to

These legal changes, once passed, would mark the first time Japan's military has engaged in overseas combat since World War II. The legislation is expected to pass the upper house after already being approved by the House of Representatives. While Japan's constitution prohibits the use of force to resolve international conflicts, except for self-defense, a new interpretation now allows for "collective self-defense," authorizing the use of force to protect allies under attack. Police are managing demonstrators in downtown Tokyo to minimize disruptions. Despite the rain, tens of thousands have been protesting in the streets, demanding the preservation of their pacifist constitution and the prime minister's removal. Despite the police presence, this unusual display of public dissent in Japan suggests a low risk of escalation. These largely citizen-led protests have continued throughout the summer.

She announced on Sunday that she would continue serving as the MP for Brighton Pavilion and intended to become more involved in active politics. Initially elected in 2008, she made history as the Green Party's first individual leader for England and Wales, departing from their earlier co-leadership model. Subsequently, in the 2010 general election, she became their first MP. She stated on Twitter that her decision to step down as leader was to pave the way for a new leader. On BBC Radio 4's Westminster Hour, she clarified that by not running for re-election as leader, she would create avenues for others to advance, solidify their standing within the party, and potentially achieve electoral victories. She emphasized the party's recent achievements, such as winning their first Westminster seat, gaining control of their first local council, and improving their overall vote share in the most recent election.

On the morning of September 24, 23-year-old Corrie McKeague, an RAF gunner based at RAF Honington, Suffolk, went missing after an evening in Bury St Edmunds. His mother, Nicola Urquhart, told the BBC's Victoria Derbyshire that it was unusual for him to disappear without contact. Urquhart added that McKeague, who was from Dunfermline, Fife, was known to take rides from strangers. CCTV footage captured him at 3:20 AM BST in Bury St Edmunds, walking alone and eating takeaway. His mobile phone signal was traced from Bury St Edmunds to Barton Mills that day, a 28-minute trip that matches the driving time between the locations, but the phone's location remains a mystery.

Regina Hungerford, a 56-year-old instructor, has denied claims that she struck a 17-year-old student who was wearing headphones in her Merthyr Tydfil College classroom. However, a disciplinary board found it probable that physical contact occurred, labeling her conduct as "unacceptable." On Thursday, the Education Workforce Council suspended her, asserting that preventing her from teaching served the "public interest." Hungerford acknowledged raising her voice and slamming a book on the desk of the "provocative and disruptive" teenager while he was listening to rap music, but maintained that she did not hit his head. Despite being acquitted of criminal assault charges related to the math lesson for students with learning disabilities, a disciplinary panel, following a November appeal, concluded that she likely made physical contact with the student's head or hand, deeming her actions "inappropriate."

Eric Morecambe took delivery of his Jensen Interceptor directly from the Jensen factory in West Bromwich on September 23, 1968, and it remained at his home until Silverstone Auctions acquired it in 2014. Following the purchase, Silverstone Auctions enlisted Jensen specialists Cropredy Bridge to refurbish the engine, brakes, and bodywork. Morecambe, who died in 1984, was the sole owner of the vehicle. Silverstone Auctions, located in Hertfordshire Warwickshire, developed a website dedicated to the car's history and restoration, including anecdotes from Morecambe's chauffeur, Mike Fountain, who sometimes drove Eric and his wife Joan. Fountain remembered the car being a tight squeeze due to its two-seater configuration, often finding Morecambe "screwed up in the back," but stressed that the Jensen was the comedian's favorite car.

N. Srinivasan, the influential BCCI president entangled in a conflict of interest due to his IPL team ownership, has temporarily relinquished his position following a Supreme Court ruling. Although elected as ICC chairman with a term starting in July, he was replaced by Sunil Gavaskar as interim BCCI president the previous month. This action stemmed from the Supreme Court's directive for the BCCI to establish a committee to probe corruption claims against Srinivasan and twelve others, including players, highlighting the court's grave view of the allegations.

A silent and poignant march, organized by those directly impacted by the Brussels airport and metro suicide bombings that claimed 32 lives, took place in Belgium, according to local news. Initially planned for the week after the March 22 attacks, the demonstration was postponed at the authorities' request due to security considerations. On Sunday, the march saw the participation of victims' relatives, paramedics, airport staff, and people from diverse religious backgrounds, all bearing flowers in remembrance of the deceased. The procession moved through Molenbeek, the home neighborhood of numerous suspected Brussels and Paris attackers, before ending at the temporary memorial close to the city's stock exchange. AFP reported that march organizer Hassan Bousetta declared, "When defenseless civilians, our fellow citizens, are murdered in a cowardly attack, all citizens must rise up to show their solidarity and abhorrence."

UEFA is contemplating introducing goal-line technology to its competitions, potentially alongside the existing additional assistant referees positioned near each goal. After Friday's talks, a verdict is anticipated in January. This technology, which has been in use in the Premier League since the 2013-14 season and by FIFA at the 2014 World Cup, is viewed positively by UEFA's general secretary, Gianni Infantino, who mentioned "logistical challenges" at a press conference in Paris. Infantino mentioned the ongoing evaluation of the technology and proposed that if adopted for Euro 2016, it would also be employed in the Champions League and Europa League the subsequent season, enhancing the current five assistant referee system. Although the final decision is scheduled for January, the executive committee appears generally supportive of the modification.

Domino's Pizza Enterprises, the Australian holder of master franchise rights for Domino's in several countries, announced a 56.7% surge in net profit to A$45.6 million, a substantial increase year-over-year. The pizza chain credited this impressive growth to its internal expansion efforts, highlighting its resilience amid global economic headwinds. Following its second upward profit revision since December, the company's stock price soared by more than 10% on Wednesday. Domino's also highlighted significant expansion in Japan, adding 48 new locations in the second half of the year, and confirmed that its Australian and New Zealand divisions are on track to exceed their goal of opening 50 new stores.

England's agonizing loss to the West Indies was sealed by Carlos Brathwaite's stunning four consecutive sixes off Ben Stokes in the last over. Despite the defeat, Cook lauded Stokes' immense talent and resilience, forecasting future success and even a potential Test score of 250. He also recognized Brathwaite's exceptional hitting ability, observing that while Stokes might regret his initial delivery, the second wasn't far off, yet still went for an impressive 94 meters. A visibly upset Cook confessed to BBC Essex that cricket rarely stirs such strong emotions in him. He expressed disappointment that the otherwise successful tournament ended negatively due to the unforeseen final over. Cook's county team, Essex, is poised to start a new era with their new coach, Chris Silverwood, on Sunday.

Police believe a man's death was likely due to a heroin overdose, potentially worsened by the presence of the more potent opioids fentanyl or carfentanyl. He was found unresponsive at a home in Fitzwilliam, close to Wakefield, on Sunday and later died in a hospital. A 43-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the incident. Det Ch Insp Stuart Spencer of West Yorkshire Police is urging heroin users, particularly those purchasing drugs illicitly, to be extremely careful when using. This warning comes after a series of deadly overdoses in Hull, Barnsley, Leeds, and Normanton, West Yorkshire, linked to "deadly batches" of heroin. In March, Cleveland Police had also connected six deaths in Stockton-on-Tees to a particular batch of heroin.

Masai Graham's witty one-liner, "My dad suggested I register for a donor card, he's a man after my own heart," secured him the coveted "Joke of the Fringe" award. A panel of 10 judges selected the best jokes from the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, followed by a public vote from a shortlist of finalists. The award, sponsored by the Dave TV channel, has been won in the past by comedians such as Tim Vine, Stewart Francis, and Zoe Lyon. Graham, a West Bromwich native and a previous finalist in 2014 and 2015, was thrilled, saying, "It's an incredible honour to land Joke of the Fringe. Not bad for someone from West Brom!" Stuart Mitchell took second place with the joke: "Why is it old people say 'there's no place like home', yet when you put them in one..." The judges each had to watch approximately 60 comedy shows.

Erika Murray, 31, was arrested Thursday night after a neighbor reported concerns about the well-being of children at her home. Detectives investigating the residence found remains inside the extremely filthy, pest-ridden property. Murray pleaded not guilty on Friday to charges including fetal death concealment, witness intimidation, and child endangerment. Her attorney, Keith Halpern, hinted at a possible mental health issue, stating after the hearing that mental illness doesn't always provide easy answers to complex situations. Worcester district attorney spokesman Tim Connolly stated that police initially went to the Blackstone home after a report that a ten-year-old boy living there had asked a neighbor how to stop a baby from crying.

Jack Whitley, who was Chelsea's goalkeeper between 1907 and 1914, played for the team during their first ever season in the highest division of English football. Even though he lived outside of London when he died, he asked to be buried in Brompton Cemetery. Because it's believed his widow couldn't afford it, the Chelsea Supporters' Trust has started a crowdfunding effort to pay for a gravestone for Whitley. Rick Glanvill, Chelsea's official historian, stressed how important a headstone would be, saying it would be incredibly meaningful. Glanvill, who has been researching the connections between the club and the cemetery, mentioned its nearness to the stadium and how, despite the burial of the club's original owner and a director there, there was a sense of something missing.

In the Sharjah match, Ben Stokes, the 24-year-old all-rounder, hurt his arm attempting a diving catch, forcing him to leave the game with a sling. The injury happened as Stokes, positioned at backward square leg, tried to catch Sarfraz Ahmed's shot off Samit Patel's bowling. Stuart Broad, Stokes's England teammate, informed BBC Sport that the injury was evident the moment Stokes landed. Broad expressed worry but emphasized the team's resilience if Stokes couldn't continue playing. Stokes, clearly in distress after the fall, received treatment and left the field using his shirt as a makeshift sling.

In April 2014, Boko Haram kidnapped 276 girls, and 21 were freed through Red Cross mediation in October. A BBC report revealed that their Christmas reunion in Chibok was marred by limitations, even though they were under government protection after their release. The girls were restricted to a politician's house, forbidden from visiting their families or attending Christmas church services. Although they were brought to a local official's home to see their parents, they were still barred from returning home. A heartbroken father said this felt like another abduction, unable to believe his daughter was so near yet unable to come home for Christmas church services. Another parent recounted a soldier seizing his phone when he tried to photograph his daughter, explaining security forces stopped him after he took their picture.

Banjong Pongphon, the mayor of Padang Besar, has been identified by police as a key suspect with considerable influence in the area where 26 bodies were discovered in mass graves last week. Padang Besar is located in the southern Songkhla province. The UN refugee agency reports that in the first three months of 2015, 25,000 migrants from Myanmar and Bangladesh traveled on smugglers' boats, a two-fold increase compared to the year before. The UNHCR also indicated that smuggler camps situated in the forests and plantations surrounding Padang Besar are the main destinations for these migrants. The autopsy results to establish the cause of death for the bodies found in the Songkhla graves are still awaited.

The police federation, advocating for 1,000 county officers, has initiated a public awareness campaign via bus and newspaper ads to illustrate how budget reductions affect conventional policing methods. They emphasize that Wiltshire Police has seen a decrease of 153 officers since 2010. Although Chief Constable Mike Veale recognizes the effects of these cuts, he insists on the force's continued commitment to community policing. The federation's "Cuts Have Consequences" campaign highlights Wiltshire's status as the area with the lowest number of officers per person in the UK, cautioning that this 16% decrease in staff leads to delayed response times, heightened vulnerability to crime at night, and a lack of accountability for drunk drivers. With £17 million already cut from the budget and a further £10 million or more anticipated, federation chairman Mike White stresses that employee expenses make up 80% of the policing budget.

Olney Rugby Club will commemorate Edgar Mobbs, the renowned England international and Northampton Saints captain, with a charity rugby match on January 24, 2015. This event pays homage to the England vs. Scotland game Mobbs organized on January 30, 1915, to enlist soldiers for his World War One battalion. The memorial match will include a game between players from the East Midlands and The 1st Battalion of the Yorkshire Regiment, alongside a contest between Olney Ladies and the Army Women's XV. Mobbs, born in Northampton in 1882 and a former Olney player, captained Northampton Rugby Football Club from 1907. Following a try against Australia in his debut in 1909, he earned seven England caps and progressed from private to battalion commander. He fought in significant battles, received the Distinguished Service Order, and was mentioned in Despatches twice before his death on July 31 during the battle of Passchendale.

A recent charity report highlights a significant disparity: just ten nations, accounting for only 2.5% of the world's GDP, are hosting more than half of the world's 21 million refugees. Amnesty International's Salil Shetty criticized wealthier nations, including the UK, for insufficient refugee intake, pointing out that since 2011, the UK has resettled around 8,000 Syrian refugees and the US only 12,000. UN data indicates that China, Russia, and Gulf states have not resettled any Syrian refugees. Conversely, Jordan, with a GDP of just 1.2% of the UK's, accommodates almost 655,000 Syrian refugees and over 2.7 million refugees in total, making it the world's largest host country, followed by Turkey (over 2.5 million), Pakistan (1.6 million), and Lebanon (over 1.5 million).

A man was caught on CCTV Monday afternoon dumping the contents of Jonathan Gwyer's food waste bin into his general waste bin outside his Whitstable home. Serco, the waste management firm responsible, apologized, calling the employee's behavior "completely unacceptable." Gwyer, who lives on Colombia Avenue, voiced his annoyance, wondering about the point of recycling and separating waste. Although he admitted the appeal of having just one bin, he mainly blamed Serco, not the individual worker, understanding the difficulties of the job and observing a recent pattern of workers being rushed and less organized. Serco issued a statement reaffirming their dedication to recycling procedures in response.

The Community Charge Debt bill aims to prevent local councils from pursuing unpaid poll tax debts. Following the Scottish independence referendum, expanded voter registration led to larger electoral rolls, which were then utilized to find individuals with outstanding poll tax obligations. The Scottish government has committed to reimbursing councils for this effort. Scotland introduced the poll tax, also known as the community charge, in 1989 under Margaret Thatcher's Conservative administration, preceding its implementation in the rest of the UK. It was abolished in 1993 after a four-year period, superseding the previous rates system. This controversial tax sparked widespread public protests. Scottish local authorities have experienced a reduction in recovered poll tax arrears, dropping below £350,000 in 2013-14, with some councils ceasing debt collection activities. Deputy First Minister John Swinney characterized the poll tax as a "hated levy" that caused hardship for Scottish communities and was broadly regarded as an impractical and universally disliked tax.

Although Libya's opposing leaders voiced a common desire to fight extremism and improve the economy, prospects for a broad accord faded as they issued separate statements on Wednesday. These meetings in the UAE between Fayez Sarraj, head of the UN-backed government, and Khalifa Haftar, the LNA commander controlling eastern Libya, occurred amidst ongoing instability since Muammar Gaddafi's ouster in 2011. Haftar has consistently hindered international efforts to resolve the conflict by refusing to acknowledge Sarraj's Government of National Accord (GNA) since its inception in 2015. A Reuters source linked to the GNA leadership revealed that while a joint statement was initially intended, each side ultimately released its own, with both calling for an end to Libya's political and economic crises.

In July 2014, a woman from Eastwood, Nottinghamshire, made multiple police reports concerning Craig Hutsby, alleging threats and breaches of his bail. Despite these warnings, Hutsby raped her the following month. An investigation by the Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) later revealed that the rape could have been prevented had arrest procedures been carried out without delay. Detective Superintendent Rachel Walker confirmed that officers were subject to misconduct hearings following the incident. The IPCC found PC Sofi Essex guilty of misconduct for failing to complete the necessary "arrest package"—the documentation required for an arrest—as instructed, a delay that the IPCC concluded enabled Hutsby to remain free and commit the rape. Furthermore, PC Joseph Lovelock was also found guilty of misconduct by the IPCC for incorrectly filling out a form pertaining to the victim, leading to a failure to identify her as high-risk and implement the necessary protection.

In front of 15,000 spectators in Berlin, South Korea's SKT1 triumphed over their compatriots, the Koo Tigers, to win the championship and the $1 million prize (£650,000). SKT1 won the final match 3-1, with the Koo Tigers being the only team to take a game from them during the entire tournament. Following the win, SKT1's Gyeong-hwan Jang stated that their consistent success against Koo was due to frequent matches and a lack of strategic variation from Koo throughout the year, making them predictable. Jang, also known as Marin, was named the most valuable player for his pivotal role in SKT1's second championship victory, especially significant as only two players remained from their 2013 championship team.

Tatenda Taibu, the 32-year-old former Zimbabwe international with 28 Test and 150 ODI appearances before retiring in 2012, surprisingly contacted Hightown Cricket Club. Nick Gordon, Hightown's publicity officer, initially dismissed it as a joke, saying he didn't believe Taibu's claim. After confirming Taibu's identity via Zimbabwean cricket connections, talks advanced, prompting Gordon to call it "a massive achievement." The ex-wicketkeeper-batsman is set to debut for the Second Division squad against Alder on April 24. Taibu responded to the club's international player advertisement, Gordon told BBC Radio Merseyside, highlighting the unexpected nature of the signing: "It's not every day that Hightown St Mary's signs a player of Tatenda's caliber. I was shocked; it was very odd."

President Obama's visit marked the first such meeting in twenty years since the normalization of relations, where he recognized the growing US-Vietnam partnership despite differing political systems. Analysts believe this strengthened relationship serves as a strategic counterweight to China's increasing influence. Occurring on the 40th anniversary of the Vietnam War, Obama recognized both the complicated past and persistent political disagreements, while underscoring the development of a mutually beneficial and respectful relationship. Mr. Trong described the talks as "cordial, constructive, positive, and frank," highlighting their evolution from former enemies to allies and comprehensive partners, expressing optimism for continued progress and inviting Obama to visit Vietnam.

Acknowledging the significant threat posed by al-Shabab, the official highlighted a recent video released by the Somalia-based group that incited attacks against shopping centers in the US, Canada, and the UK. He cited al-Shabab's prior claim of responsibility for the 2013 Westgate mall attack in Nairobi, which resulted in 67 fatalities. In an interview with CNN, he characterized the threat as "a new phase" of terrorism, characterized by increased attacks from "independent actors in their homelands." While stressing the importance of taking any terrorist group's call for specific attacks seriously, he clarified that he was not advising people to stay away from the malls mentioned by the militants. The video featured a masked man with a British accent urging al-Shabab supporters to target "American or..." locations.

After conferring with Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny, the British Prime Minister described the UK and Ireland as "close friends," with Kenny echoing his contentment with their growing bond. Cameron is set to join the Queen and Duke of Edinburgh at a state dinner during their historic four-day visit—the first by a British monarch since Ireland's independence. Cameron stressed that the Queen's presence underscores the possibility of an even more robust relationship, built upon trade, investment, economic partnerships, and collaborative opportunities as neighbors. He also acknowledged the Queen's "great understanding" of the intricate shared history between the UK and Ireland. While Cameron and Kenny previously met in Downing Street in April, this is their first meeting in Ireland since Kenny became Taoiseach in March.

In response to the president's stance on issues like climate change, especially his denial of its existence, parody accounts mimicking organizations like NASA and the Environmental Protection Agency have surfaced. One such account, @RogueNASA, presents itself as an unofficial NASA "Resistance" group, emphasizing its autonomy from both the agency and the government while vowing to deliver factual information with a satirical edge. Likewise, @ActualEPAFacts, a counterpart to the official EPA account, informed BBC News of its commitment to continue disseminating factual data on climate change and scientific research throughout the Trump administration. The individuals behind this account, identifying themselves as three EPA employees, cited a communication restriction preventing them from openly discussing their research as their motivation. Reports suggest the Trump administration has sought to limit public discourse from specific government entities, including the EPA, whose official Twitter account has remained dormant since the day preceding Trump's inauguration.

Although the Labour party officially supports remaining in the EU, doubts persist about Jeremy Corbyn's commitment to the cause, given his history of EU skepticism. Worried Labour MPs fear that Corbyn's lukewarm support could negatively impact the referendum result. A spokesperson stated that Corbyn intends to give a major speech on the issue in the near future. During a visit to Dagenham, Corbyn admitted the EU needs reform but emphasized the importance of European cooperation, echoing Labour's current campaign message. He reiterated Labour's commitment to "social justice across Europe," citing the social chapter and Working Time Directive, and mentioned efforts to gain support from European socialist parties. Notably, Corbyn had previously kept the door open to leaving the EU during his leadership campaign.

At Preston Crown Court, Matthew Eteson, 42, is being tried for manslaughter by gross negligence in connection with the deaths of Kelly Webster, 36, and her daughter, Lauren Thornton. The prosecution, led by Graham Reeds QC, alleges that the tragic event occurred on April 1, 2013, during an Easter break to Windermere. Eteson is accused of relocating a generator from outside the boat to power a 1kW fan heater within the cabin while the victims slept. The court was informed that the carbon monoxide detectors were non-functional, leaving the mother and daughter from Leyland, Lancashire, without warning as the lethal gas accumulated. They were found dead in their beds on the Arniston, a used Bayliner 285 motor cruiser, with fatal levels of carbon monoxide in their bodies.

While performing standard upkeep on Reactor Three, EDF Energy detected fissures in three graphite bricks. The company clarified that this situation, akin to "keyway root cracking" identified in the adjacent reactor in the previous year, presents no danger to safety and does not impede the reactor's functionality. EDF Energy highlighted that this disclosure underscores their commitment to being transparent and communicative. Station head Colin Weir confirmed that nuclear safety remains paramount and that considerable safety buffers exist to accommodate the condition of the graphite bricks. He also noted that the permissible degree of cracking is substantially lower than the level that would lead to adverse effects.

The company behind the London Array wind farm has launched a three-year study to determine how additional turbines might affect red-throated divers. This follows their initial proposal to expand the wind farm, located off the coasts of Kent and Essex, to a total of 341 turbines. The area provides winter habitat for around 6,500 red-throated divers, representing at least a third of the UK's entire population. London Array has now formally requested The Crown Estate to terminate the lease for the planned second phase and has also relinquished the reserved grid capacity at the National Grid substation in Graveney, Kent. The wind farm project, approved in 2006 and situated 10 miles north of Ramsgate, Kent, was conditional upon protecting red-throated divers during the second phase expansion, which envisioned adding 166 turbines. The RSPB had previously expressed worries that the expansion could displace the bird population from the outer Thames estuary. According to Mike, London Array's general manager,

McClarty's choice to remain independent, despite the opportunity to give the UUP two executive positions, secures a seat for Alliance, as the UUP now only holds one post. McClarty cited his promise to supporters who wished him to stay independent as the reason, denying self-interest despite the potential for a ministerial role. He also voiced concerns about the UUP's structure, characterizing it as a disunited group of associations without strong central direction. BBC's Gareth Gordon highlighted that McClarty, who left the Ulster Unionists in January following his deselection, denied acting out of revenge, though he admitted his decision would likely harm his former party.

Robert Hannigan stepped down as director of GCHQ in 2017, a post he'd held from 2014, explaining that the demands of the role were impacting his family after 20 years of government work. He voiced satisfaction with his achievements at GCHQ, and then-Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson recognized his efforts to update national security protections against terrorism. Before heading GCHQ, Hannigan was the director general of defense and intelligence at the Foreign Office. In his resignation letter, he emphasized GCHQ's success in protecting lives at home and abroad, but argued that fresh leadership was needed to steer the agency in the future.

IHS reported that the area controlled by IS had shrunk to 68,300 sq km (26,370 sq miles) since the declaration of its "caliphate" two years earlier. The report indicated that this loss of territory has led IS to intensify its attacks on civilians in the Middle East and Europe, a pattern expected to persist. As an example, a recent IS suicide bombing in Baghdad resulted in almost 300 deaths, happening shortly after the Iraqi government proclaimed the full liberation of Falluja, located west of Baghdad. IHS further stated that in January 2015, six months after its declaration, IS held around 90,800 sq km of Iraqi and Syrian land. By the end of that year, this had fallen by 12,800 sq km to 78,000 sq km, a 14% reduction. Subsequently, IS has lost another 9,700 sq km, leaving them with control over 68,300 sq km.

David Poole, 38, pleaded guilty at Cardiff Crown Court to entrapping 27-year-old Adnan Khalid, who was accused of grooming a 14-year-old. Poole was charged with perjury during Khalid's trial, which Judge Thomas Crowther QC ultimately halted, acquitting Khalid, from Porth, Rhondda Cynon Taff. Judge Crowther also condemned H Division, Poole's paedophile hunter group, for causing the trial's failure. Poole, of Hereford, created a fake profile named Chloe on Plenty of Fish, pretending to be a 14-year-old, and arranged a meeting with Khalid in Cardiff following secretly recorded WhatsApp conversations. Khalid, who denied the charges, stated he believed he was communicating with a woman over 18. Judge Crowther cited Poole's lateness to court and his subsequent false statement about providing photographic evidence to the police as reasons for his criticism.

Jamie Vardy, aged 29, postponed his wedding plans twice to play in Euro 2016, rescheduling it from the previous year and then again from its original June date. Roy Hodgson, England's coach, understood Vardy's need to take leave for his wedding. After his winning goal in England's 2-1 win against Turkey on Sunday, Vardy stated he would leave on Wednesday but return to training afterwards. Hodgson backed Vardy's place on the team, highlighting the importance of evaluating other players too. Vardy, who scored an impressive 24 Premier League goals during Leicester's title-winning season, started the Turkey match at the Etihad Stadium on the left of the attacking front three, before moving centrally and scoring the winning goal after Harry Kane's initial goal.

To reduce the number of doctor visits and the overuse of antibiotics, NHS England has launched a walk-in service projected to alleviate pressure on GPs and potentially save the NHS millions each year. However, pharmacies worry that funding cuts could jeopardize the program's effectiveness. The Sore Throat Test and Treat service, first trialed in 35 Boots pharmacies, differentiates between viral infections, which do not respond to antibiotics, and bacterial infections. Using a rapid throat swab test that analyzes sugars on the tongue, the service provides results in just five minutes, allowing pharmacists to prescribe antibiotics directly to suitable patients, thereby avoiding the need for a GP appointment. NHS chief executive Simon Stevens has announced the program will be rolled out nationally next year, with Dr. Adam Roberts, a University College London microbiologist specializing in antibiotic resistance, calling it "quite an innovative step."

Following a Russian-brokered agreement with "moderate" opposition forces, a ceasefire commenced in Eastern Ghouta, though its sustainability remains questionable according to analysts. Eastern Ghouta was already part of a "de-escalation zone" established in May through a deal between Russia, Iran, and Turkey. The Syrian military declared the ceasefire's commencement at noon local time on Saturday (09:00 GMT), cautioning that any breaches would be met with a proportional reaction. Faylaq al-Rahman, an insurgent group, expressed support for the truce and urged the government to respect it. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported isolated shelling incidents after the ceasefire's implementation, but no major clashes. This development occurred after Russia publicized a separate agreement with rebels in Cairo concerning the safe zone's operational specifics.

In August 2016, the pilot of an A320 flying south of Brookmans Park narrowly avoided a mid-air collision with a white quadcopter drone that "flashed past" the aircraft. The UK Airprox Board concluded that the near miss was averted solely by chance, given the lack of time for evasive action. Air traffic control confirmed the pilot's report of an object passing overhead north of Potters Bar around 18:45 BST on August 15, 2016. While air traffic control mentioned another aircraft flying above, the pilot specified that the object was under a meter in size, with a red and white body and red and blue stripes on two rotor arms. Drone operators are legally required to comply with the regulations governing small unmanned aircraft operations as stipulated in the Air Navigation Order (ANO) 2016.

The hashtag #penuriecarburantdansunfilm, or "fuel shortage in a film," exploded on French Twitter on Tuesday, exceeding 5,000 tweets and becoming a top trending topic. This surge in activity was triggered by strikes affecting all eight of France's oil refineries in response to new labor laws, resulting in reports that around 20% of French gas stations are either dry or facing supply issues. French social media users cleverly referenced films like Total Recall, alluding to the French oil and gas company Total, while others playfully modified titles like Pulp Fiction into Pump Friction to satirize the current fuel shortage.

Following a cheating scandal involving 54 student officers, an inquiry at the Garverville college in east Belfast exposed a highly punitive and "pseudo-militaristic" atmosphere. As a result, the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has committed to enacting 50 suggested reforms. Chief Constable George Hamilton and other high-ranking PSNI leaders are set to confer with the Policing Board to deliberate on a strategy for resolving the problems identified. Immediate adjustments to the 22-week training course will include eliminating student marches between sites and discontinuing military-style "show parades" employed as a form of discipline. Furthermore, student "squads" will be renamed "classes." The PSNI's plan details 34 modifications slated to be finished by the conclusion of the subsequent March.

The royal couple's tour began at the Seamus Heaney Homeplace in Bellaghy, where they met members of the poet's family. Their schedule includes visits to Londonderry, Belfast, and County Down. In Bellaghy, they toured the visitor's centre, a key source of inspiration for much of Heaney's renowned poetry. Prince Charles, a long-standing admirer of the Nobel Prize winner, had previously encountered Heaney on several occasions. After the Bellaghy stop, they visited the North West Cancer Centre at Altnagelvin Hospital in Londonderry, speaking with both staff and patients. The day concluded with their attendance at a musical performance held at Hillsborough Castle in County Down on Tuesday evening.

Calls for modernizing the Winnington Turn Bridge, a Grade II listed, single-lane swing bridge built in 1908 across the River Weaver Navigation in Northwich, are intensifying due to severe rush hour traffic. Local representatives, including parish councillors and MP George Osborne, are advocating for upgrades, prompting Cheshire West and Chester Council to launch a feasibility study. This early electrically operated swing bridge, located on the A533 and providing access to the M56, is a major source of traffic congestion. According to Dilys Hooper, Chair of Barnton Parish Council, delays can reach 40 minutes during peak hours, creating "mayhem," and she fears the planned construction of at least 4,300 new homes in Northwich will exacerbate the bridge's traffic problems.

Disguised as police, eight individuals infiltrated the airport perimeter on Monday night, boarded a Swiss-bound aircraft, and stole approximately $50 million (Â£32 million; 37 million euros) in gems from the cargo area. They then escaped through the same security breach. A torched vehicle was later found nearby. Caroline De Wolf of the Antwerp World Diamond Centre characterized the stolen goods as "a gigantic sum." While Belgian state media initially reported 350 million euros ($468 million), an anonymous Antwerp center source confirmed the theft as "one of the biggest" on record, identifying the stolen items as "rough stones" being transported from Antwerp, the world's foremost diamond trading hub, to Zurich.

In 2010, Cardiff grappled with Wales' most significant budget deficit, totaling £494 million or £1,450 per inhabitant. While Cardiff's shortfall was substantial, Merthyr Tydfil's per capita deficit was the highest in the UK, reaching £2,268. Local councils challenged the report, claiming they had already taken steps to improve pension affordability. The Taxpayers Alliance analyzed 101 UK local government pension schemes, utilizing financial data and actuarial projections from 2010-11 to assess their funding levels. The Alliance contended that these defined benefit plans were "inflexible and overly expensive," necessitating immediate reform, and urged councils to take corrective measures.

The delayed 2012 badger cull cost £2.5 million, with subsequent expenses of £9.8 million in 2013 and £4.5 million in 2014. Critics have labeled the cull a "disastrous" and growing financial strain on taxpayers. Defra reported a 50% reduction in operational costs between 2013 and 2014, attributed to greater financial contributions from farmers. Bovine TB, a badger-borne disease that significantly threatens cattle farming, necessitates routine cattle testing and the culling of infected animals; in England during 2014, 26,413 cattle were slaughtered after testing positive for TB. Concerns persist about the effectiveness of badger culls in curbing TB transmission, as well as the ethical implications of nighttime badger shootings.
